summary:
With the season just days away, most clubs are putting the finishing touches to their pre-season preparations rather than playing competitive football. A few standout stories emerged this week.

Eccleshall, who dominated last season with 74 points, are clearly building for another strong challenge. They've confirmed their captain and vice-captains, with Nicky Parker staying despite reported interest from other clubs, and Levi Hunter and Adam Whitehouse stepping into leadership roles. The squad looks settled heading into the campaign.

Stafford Town had an emphatic final friendly, thumping Cradley Town 6-3 at home. Multiple players got on the scoresheet, including two from Lynch, suggesting their attacking play is sharp. They've also signed a couple of development players to their first team, with young goalkeeper Luke Crowther making his debut in that match.

New Mills have taken a more measured pre-season, losing their final two friendlies to Glossop North End and Trafford, though both opponents play a level above them. They're focusing on getting valuable minutes in the tank and appear settled with their new management team and squad.

Telford Town bounced back from early going behind, drawing 2-2 with Stourport Swifts after coming from a goal down, showing decent character and resilience in a warm-weather friendly.

Foley Meir have been remarkably active in the transfer window, announcing numerous signings in quick succession across several days. They're clearly building a squad with experience, bringing in players from Macclesfield, Crewe Alexandra, and other clubs, suggesting their recruitment strategy is well-advanced.

The division looks competitive, with several clubs (Eccleshall particularly) appearing well-organised and strong heading into opening weekend.
